::: {.callout-important}
## Synthetic data

The data is synthetic. Aurora Lending Group is a fictional company.
:::

This file has one way to answer each prompt in [`aurora-eda.qmd`](aurora-eda.qmd). Posit Assistant may write different code. Compare the numbers, not the code.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
source("athena.R")

whoami()
```

## 1. Orient

```{r}
#| label: tables
athena_query("
  SELECT table_name
  FROM information_schema.tables
  WHERE table_schema = 'aurora_lending'
  ORDER BY table_name
")
```

`fct_loan_performance` has one row per loan. It joins to `dim_borrower` on `borrower_id`, to `dim_loan_product` on `product_id`, and to `dim_date` on `origination_date_key`.

## 2. Load the loan book

```{r}
#| label: load
loans <- athena_query("
  SELECT f.loan_id,
         f.origination_date,
         f.principal_amount,
         f.outstanding_balance,
         f.apr,
         f.dti,
         f.fico_at_origination,
         f.months_on_book,
         f.delinquency_days,
         f.charged_off,
         p.product_name,
         p.purpose,
         p.term_months,
         b.state,
         b.income_band,
         b.homeownership,
         b.employment_length_years
  FROM fct_loan_performance f
  JOIN dim_loan_product p ON p.product_id = f.product_id
  JOIN dim_borrower b ON b.borrower_id = f.borrower_id
")

glimpse(loans)
```

## 3. Check the data

```{r}
#| label: checks
tibble(
  check = c(
    "Loans",
    "Missing values, any column",
    "Duplicate loan IDs",
    "FICO outside 300-850",
    "Negative outstanding balance",
    "APR outside 0-100% (stored as a fraction)"
  ),
  result = c(
    nrow(loans),
    sum(is.na(loans)),
    sum(duplicated(loans$loan_id)),
    sum(loans$fico_at_origination < 300 | loans$fico_at_origination > 850),
    sum(loans$outstanding_balance < 0),
    sum(loans$apr < 0 | loans$apr > 1)
  )
)
```

## 4. Where is the risk?

The FICO bands match the Portfolio Risk Review report. They are closed on the right, so a score of 620 falls in 580-619.

```{r}
#| label: bands
loans <- loans |>
  mutate(
    fico_band = cut(
      fico_at_origination,
      breaks = c(579, 620, 660, 700, 740, 780, 850),
      labels = c("580-619", "620-659", "660-699", "700-739", "740-779", "780+")
    ),
    vintage = as.integer(format(as.Date(origination_date), "%Y"))
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: by-product
by_product <- loans |>
  summarise(loans = n(), charge_off_rate = mean(charged_off), .by = product_name) |>
  arrange(desc(charge_off_rate))

by_product

ggplot(by_product, aes(charge_off_rate, reorder(product_name, charge_off_rate))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#447099") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Charge-off rate by loan product", x = "Charge-off rate", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
#| label: by-fico
by_fico <- loans |>
  summarise(loans = n(), charge_off_rate = mean(charged_off), .by = fico_band) |>
  arrange(fico_band)

by_fico

ggplot(by_fico, aes(fico_band, charge_off_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#447099") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Charge-off rate by FICO band at origination",
       x = "FICO at origination", y = "Charge-off rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Ask a follow-up

```{r}
#| label: product-within-fico
#| fig-height: 5
product_fico <- loans |>
  summarise(loans = n(), charge_off_rate = mean(charged_off),
            .by = c(product_name, fico_band))

ggplot(product_fico, aes(fico_band, reorder(product_name, charge_off_rate), fill = charge_off_rate)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(charge_off_rate, accuracy = 1)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F3F6F8", high = "#447099", labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Charge-off rate by product within each FICO band",
       x = "FICO at origination", y = NULL, fill = "Charge-off rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

Small business loans have the highest charge-off rate in every FICO band, from about 38% at 580-619 to about 5% at 780+. FICO doesn't explain the product's risk: it carries risk of its own.

## 6. Account for time on book

```{r}
#| label: by-vintage
by_vintage <- loans |>
  summarise(loans = n(), charge_off_rate = mean(charged_off),
            months_on_book = median(months_on_book), .by = vintage) |>
  arrange(vintage)

by_vintage

ggplot(by_vintage, aes(vintage, charge_off_rate)) +
  geom_line(color = "#447099", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#447099") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "Charge-off rate by origination year",
       x = "Origination year", y = "Charge-off rate") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The charge-off rate is about 10% in every origination year, even though 2025 loans have a median of only 5 months on book. In a real loan book, recent years usually look safer only because they are young, so compare years at the same months on book before you draw a conclusion.
